calls.head: Minnesota feeds on loose pucks
calls.body: Buffalo gives up more dangerous chances after losing the puck than most (23rd of 32 at avoiding breakdowns). Minnesota ranks 9th for chances off turnovers.
calls.call: At least its usual 7.5% of Minnesota’s 5-on-5 chances come right after winning the puck.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: 2.2% of Minnesota’s 5-on-5 chances came right after winning the puck, against its usual 7.5%.

calls.head: Buffalo hunts better looks than Minnesota
calls.body: On shot quality, Buffalo sits 10th of 32, at the point-blank end of the scale. Minnesota is 23rd, at the perimeter end.
calls.call: Buffalo’s shots are more dangerous on average than Minnesota’s.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: On how dangerous the average unblocked shot was, Buffalo had 1 goal per 13.2 shots and Minnesota 1 goal per 19.0 shots. Coming in, Buffalo was at 1 goal per 15.4 shots and Minnesota at 1 goal per 16.3 shots.
calls.usual: BUF 1 goal per 15.4 shots · MIN 1 goal per 16.3 shots
calls.tonight: BUF 1 goal per 13.2 shots · MIN 1 goal per 19.0 shots

BUF.head: We had this close to even (56% for Buffalo), and Buffalo came through.

MIN.head: We had this close to even (44% for Minnesota), and it went Buffalo’s way.

surprises.head: Buffalo hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Buffalo’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 47, against its usual 95 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 20 games.

surprises.head: Buffalo shut down Minnesota’s power play
surprises.body: Minnesota’s power play created 2.5 expected goals per 60, against its usual 7.5 and a league average of 7.5. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 20 games.
